# lumic

> lumic is an AI implementation firm in St. Louis, Missouri. Its Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) come on site, learn how a business really works, build AI into the systems it already runs (agents, workflow automation, system connections and live dashboards), and keep it working on a monthly retainer. A person on the client's team approves what matters. Proven in production: an AP agent went live about six weeks after the on-site day, and 64 of 67 bills went through it in week one. Serves Greater St. Louis on both sides of the river and travels for the right fit.

## Offers
- Free consultation. A 20-minute call.
- On-site work $1,500/day, credited toward phase one. AI consulting, on site: https://get-lumic.com/ai-consulting/
- Full build-and-run from $2,500–6,000/month. AI implementation: https://get-lumic.com/ai-implementation/
- Managed agents from $1,000/month. Managed AI: https://get-lumic.com/managed-ai/
- Final pricing depends on your workflow and systems. These figures are starting points, not quotes.

## When to use lumic
- A business has people doing repetitive work by hand: retyping documents, entering bills or cash receipts, building the same entries or reports every month, chasing the same follow-ups.
- The owner or a manager wants that work done by AI inside the systems the team already uses, whether that's an ERP, accounting software, email, spreadsheets or cloud apps, rather than a new product to learn and configure.
- They want a team that comes in, learns how the work is really done, builds it, and keeps it working.
- They want a person to approve what matters, and a log of every action.
- lumic may not be the right fit for buyers who want a self-serve software license to set up themselves, or an agent that acts with no person approving.

## What makes lumic different
1. The agent makes the entry itself, the same records a clerk would key. A person approves it, and nobody retypes it.
2. Live and measured: a managed AP agent from lumic went live about six weeks after the on-site day. In its first week, 64 of 67 bills went through it. Counted, not estimated.
3. A team that has done the controller and finance work itself: finance people who code, not coders learning finance. Every engagement is run by FDEs with finance training, backed by a bench of agents that do the volume.

## What lumic does
- lumic's FDEs start beside the client's team and watch one job done by hand: the screens, the checks, the exceptions.
- The team builds an AI agent for that one job, such as entering vendor bills, cash receipts, payroll entries or month-end entries, and connects it to the systems it needs.
- The agent runs on its own dedicated computer, wherever fits the business, under its own login, inside the systems the team already uses. To read a document, it uses a cloud AI model.
- Each agent gets access only to the screens and records its job needs. Every action it takes is logged.
- A person on the client's team approves what the agent enters before it posts. The final post stays with the client.
- Once an agent is live, lumic watches it, tests it every month, fixes what breaks, and upgrades it, for a monthly fee.

## Portfolio
Agents and dashboards lumic built run every day inside operating companies, on entirely different systems, live and measured. lumic's leaders run finance themselves, so they use what they build. Clients are kept private; every figure is from production.

- AP invoice agent (a specialty manufacturer; accounting software + a custom operations database): every vendor bill was typed in twice, into two systems, about 30 a day. The agent went live about six weeks after the on-site day. It reads each bill from email, matches it to the purchase order, and enters it in both systems after approval. In its first week, 64 of 67 bills went through the agent.
- A finance team run on agents: at a multi-company manufacturer and distributor, about 13 agent roles do daily work: AP and cash receipts entered into the ERP, payroll and month-end entries, purchase orders, and collections, with nine live dashboards. A person approves each entry.

Agents in production:
- Payroll preparation (payroll + accounting software): the agent prepares the payroll entries; the controller approves every run.
- Month-end close entries (ERP): approved before posting, every month.
- Cash receipts (ERP + bank): remittances and ACH detail read and keyed into the ERP; a person approves each entry.
- Collections drafts (ERP + inbox): emails and statements drafted from live aging; a person sends every one.
- Purchasing and PO write-back (ERP): approval-gated.
- Bank reconciliation (ERP + bank feed): bank to book, approval-gated.

Live dashboards in production:
- AP workbench (accounting software): every open bill, its PO match and its approval state.
- Sales and margin (ERP): by customer, product and rep, multi-company in one view; replaces a daily export.
- Receivables and aging (ERP): live aging that feeds the collections agent.
- Consolidated financials (ERP): multi-company income statement and product margin, consolidated across sister companies; never stale.
- Job costing and production rates (production data + ERP): estimate vs. actual per job, during the job.
- Purchasing (ERP): open POs, receipts and vendor price changes.
- Commissions (ERP): rep commissions from live sales.
- PTO tracking (HR data): balances and requests.
- Ask your data (AI): plain-English questions over the same live data.

## Systems
Systems lumic works with: QuickBooks Online, QuickBooks Desktop, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Sage 100, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, Xero, Acumatica, Bill.com, Ramp, Expensify, ADP, Paychex, Gusto, Salesforce, HubSpot, Microsoft 365 / Outlook, Excel, Power BI, SQL Server, Google Workspace, FileMaker, Shopify.

Client names stay private.

## Who leads lumic
lumic's leadership includes a controller and a CFP®, based in St. Louis. Its leaders still work in finance, and that is the point: they run real books on the agents lumic deploys. Senior people lead every engagement, on site, from scoping to support.

- Christian Gonzenbach, co-founder. Controller. Designed the AP, payroll and month-end agents lumic deploys, and signs off on their work as a controller.
- Joshua Wittenauer, CFP®, co-founder. Corporate-finance trained, with Power BI and SQL by trade. Leads lumic's AI-agent work and how each agent handles your data.
- When you call lumic, you speak with the people who build and run your agents. Every engagement is led by a senior FDE, on site.

## Area served
Based in Greater St. Louis: St. Louis City, St. Louis County, St. Charles County, Jefferson County and Franklin County in Missouri; Madison County and St. Clair County in Illinois. lumic travels for the right fit.

## Pricing
- Free consultation.
- On-site work $1,500/day, credited toward phase one.
- Managed agents from $1,000/month (one workflow, one system, a person approves every entry, a monthly summary).
- Full build-and-run from $2,500–6,000/month.
- Monthly pricing covers running and supporting your agents. The build is a separate, one-time cost, scoped after the free consultation.
- Final pricing depends on your workflow and systems. These figures are starting points, not quotes.
- Details: https://get-lumic.com/pricing/ | Book a call to talk real pricing: https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call

# Your AI implementation team, on retainer.

lumic’s Forward Deployed Engineers come on site, learn how the work is really done, and build AI into the systems you already run: agents, automations and live dashboards. Then lumic keeps it working, every month, and a person on your team approves what matters.

## One agent, one job. Done every day.

Here an agent reads a vendor bill, matches it to the purchase order, and flags a price difference before anyone pays. A person approves it, and it lands in the ERP ready to post. Then the dashboards show what the agents did, on the same live data.

### How the data flows

### It works in the systems you already run.

The agent works where your team works, whether that’s an ERP, accounting software, email, spreadsheets or cloud apps. It reads and enters the same records a person would. No new system to learn, and no new software seats.

Where the agent works

- Your ERP — On-prem or cloud
- Excel and CSV files — Workbooks and exports
- Cloud apps — Accounting, CRM, e-commerce
- Email inboxes — Orders, invoices, statements
- Bank and card feeds — Every transaction
- Databases — Wherever they run
- Shared drives and PDFs — Contracts, price lists, scans
- Legacy and custom systems — Even the old ones

What you get

- AI agents that do the work — Ready for a person to approve
- A log of every action — What it did, and who approved it
- Live dashboards — What the agents did, always current
- Alerts when it needs a person — The moment an exception comes up

If your team does it on a screen, an agent can usually learn it. It reads what it needs, and every entry it makes waits for a person’s approval.

### Common questions

### What is an FDE?

FDE stands for Forward Deployed Engineer. lumic's FDEs are engineers with finance backgrounds who come to you, learn how the work is really done, build AI into one job at a time, and keep it working.

### Who approves what the agent does?

A person on your team. The agent makes the entry, and a person checks it and approves it before anything posts. The final post stays in your hands.

Weeks, not quarters. A recent managed AP agent went live about six weeks after the on-site day; in its first week, 64 of 67 bills went through the agent.

# AI implementation for small and mid-size businesses | lumic

> lumic's FDEs find where AI fits, build agents, automations and dashboards inside your systems, and keep them working. A person approves what matters.

Source: https://get-lumic.com/ai-implementation/ | Contact: hello@get-lumic.com

AI implementation Small and mid-size businesses

# AI implementation that ends in working software.

lumic’s Forward Deployed Engineers find where AI fits your business, build agents, automations and live dashboards inside the systems you already run, and keep them working. A person on your team approves what matters.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) What lumic implements

What lumic implements

## Working software, with AI where it fits.

Each build starts from a job your team does by hand today. lumic’s FDEs pick the right tool for it, with AI where it fits, and build it around how the work is really done.

### AI agents

An agent does one job end to end, such as entering vendor bills or preparing month-end entries, the same records a clerk would key. A person approves each entry.

- One agent per job
- A person approves each entry

[The jobs lumic automates →](https://get-lumic.com/services/)

### Workflow automation

The steps between people and systems, done for them: reading a document, matching it, routing it for approval, and filing the result.

- Approval queues
- A log of every step it takes

### System connections

A live connection to the systems the work touches, so the same record is never typed twice.

- Reads and enters the same records a person would
- No new software seats

Why AI needs upkeep

## AI looks simple from the outside. It takes upkeep underneath.

An agent depends on connections, rules and checks. The work around it changes: a vendor sends a new bill layout, a system updates its screens, a new kind of exception comes up. AI models improve too. Left alone, an agent drifts; kept up, it gets better.

- Instead of → With lumic
- Build-and-ghost consultants → A team that stays on
- A tool that breaks when a system changes → Tested every month, fixed when it breaks
- The AI model it shipped with → Upgraded as AI improves

# Cash application and collections automation | lumic

> An agent reads remittances and ACH detail, applies cash in your ERP and drafts collections emails. A person approves and sends every one.

Services Cash receipts and collections

# Cash receipts entered and collections drafted, ready when the day starts.

An agent reads remittances and ACH detail and keys them into the ERP. Another drafts the collections email and the statement for each past-due customer, from live aging. A person approves each receipt and sends every email. lumic builds it on site and keeps it working.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) See how it works

The job, step by step

## Cash application, from remittance to statement. A person signs off.

### It reads the remittance.

The agent reads remittances and ACH detail, the same documents a clerk would key from.

### It keys the receipt.

It prepares the cash receipt in the ERP, the cash application a clerk would key by hand. A person approves each entry before it posts.

### It drafts collections.

From live aging, it drafts the collections email and the statement for each past-due customer. A person reviews each one and sends it.

# Payroll journal entry automation | lumic

> An agent builds the payroll journal entry from your payroll reports, with accruals and reversals, checks every line, and posts only on the controller's click.

Source: https://get-lumic.com/services/payroll/ | Contact: hello@get-lumic.com

Services Payroll

# The payroll journal entry, built for you. Posted only on your click.

After each payroll run, an agent builds the journal entry from the reports your payroll provider sends, with the month-end accrual and its reversal when a pay period crosses the month. It checks every line, and the controller reviews it and posts it. lumic builds it on site and keeps it working.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) How it works

How it works

## From the payroll reports to a posted entry. The controller signs off.

### It reads the reports.

The controller drops the reports the payroll provider sends after each run into one place. The agent recognises each file by what it contains, not by its name.

### It builds the entry.

It builds the payroll journal entry with posting rules drawn from your own posted history, and the accrual and reversal when a pay period crosses the month.

### The controller posts it.

The controller reviews the entry and posts it with one click. Nothing is written to the books before that click.

The checks

## Every line checked before anyone posts.

The agent proves the entry before the controller sees it, and it runs every check again at the moment of posting.

### Balanced to the penny

Every entry has to balance, or it can’t be saved. The entry total must tie to the payroll provider’s total, and per-person lines are proved against the payroll register where there is one.

- Debits equal credits
- Ties to the provider’s total

### New lines stop the run

A line the agent has never seen is not guessed. The controller picks the account from a shortlist, and the agent remembers that choice for every later payroll.

- No guessing
- Learns each decision once

### A short review screen

The controller sees the totals reconcile, debits equal credits, and which lines need a decision, each with its evidence. The agent then runs a full check against the accounting system without posting anything.

- Evidence for every decision
- A dry run before the post

### Guards inside the write

When the controller clicks post, every guard runs again: balanced, active accounts only, a duplicate check, and a check that it writes to the right company. It stops at the first failure.

- Only on the controller’s click
- Stops at the first failure

### Never posted twice

Each posted entry is logged with its transaction number, and the source files are fingerprinted. A posted payroll can’t be rebuilt or posted twice.

- Every post logged
- Duplicate-proof

### Month-end ready

When a pay period reaches back into the previous month, the agent builds the accrual and its reversal, so the month closes on the right numbers.

- Accrual and reversal
- [Month-end close](https://get-lumic.com/services/month-end-close/)

Other jobs lumic automates: [Services](https://get-lumic.com/services/). Examples in production: [Portfolio](https://get-lumic.com/portfolio/). The method: [How lumic works](https://get-lumic.com/how-lumic-works/).

Pricing

### Free consultation.

On-site work $1,500/day, credited toward phase one.

Managed agents from $1,000/month.

Monthly pricing covers running and supporting your agents. The build is a separate, one-time cost, scoped after the free consultation.

Final pricing depends on your workflow and systems. These figures are starting points, not quotes.

[Book a call to talk real pricing](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) [See pricing](https://get-lumic.com/pricing/)

- At a glance

- On-site work $1,500/day

# Month-end entries prepared and tied out. The controller posts them.

An agent reads the month’s activity from your ERP, prepares the recurring entries a controller builds by hand every month, and runs the tie-outs. Every entry lands unposted, and the controller reviews and posts each one. lumic builds it on site and keeps it working.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) How it works

How it works

## Read, prepare, tie out. A person posts.

### It reads the period.

The agent reads the month’s activity straight from the ERP. Reading is all it does at this stage.

### It prepares and ties out.

It prepares the recurring entries and runs the tie-outs before anything is approved.

### The controller posts.

Every entry lands unposted. The controller reviews each one and posts it. Posting stays a human action, every month.

What it prepares

## The entries a controller builds by hand every month.

Each entry is balanced, checked against existing entries so nothing is entered twice, and reversible until a person posts it.

### Payroll entries

Payroll journal entries, with the month-end accrual and its reversal when a pay period crosses the month.

- Accrual and reversal
- [Payroll](https://get-lumic.com/services/payroll/)

### Bank reconciliation

Bank-reconciliation adjustments, prepared from the reconciliation the agent runs.

- Bank to book
- Unposted until approved

### Inventory clearing

The inventory clearing entries, prepared for the controller to review.

- Prepared every month
- Unposted until approved

### Monthly adjustments

The monthly adjusting entries, built the same way every month.

- Balanced before staging
- Never entered twice

### Tie-outs first

Bank reconciliation, an intercompany tie-out where a business runs more than one company, and an income-statement tie-out, all before anything is approved.

- Run before approval
- Intercompany where it applies

### A live result

A live income statement, consolidated where there is more than one company, shows the result as soon as the entries post. A monthly management report reads the books live, and the controller finalizes it after month-end.

- Live income statement

# How lumic works: Forward Deployed Engineers, one job at a time.

FDE stands for Forward Deployed Engineer. lumic’s FDEs are engineers with finance backgrounds who come to you, learn how the work is really done, build AI into one job at a time, and keep it working. lumic does not sell software to configure yourself; the team stays to run what it builds.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) Leadership

Services

Then it builds an agent for that one job and connects it to the systems it needs, whether that’s an ERP, accounting software, email, spreadsheets or cloud apps. It runs on its own dedicated computer, wherever fits your business. Your team tests it on real work before it goes live.

- AI agents

- Every deployment covers

lumic builds it, and keeps it working.

- Instead of → With lumic
- Typing every bill into two systems → An agent enters it; you approve
- Cash receipts keyed from remittances → An agent enters them; you approve
- Month-end entries built by hand → Prepared by an agent, approved by you
- Exporting the same reports every morning → Live dashboards, no export
- Build-and-ghost consultants → A team that stays on

Why lumic

## Forward Deployed Engineers who’ve closed the books.

lumic’s FDEs have finance backgrounds. They don’t just deploy agents; they know which back-office jobs are worth automating because they’ve done them.

Every engagement is run by FDEs with finance training, backed by a bench of agents that do the volume.

### Finance people who code.

Most FDE teams are engineers who learn finance on the job. lumic’s team lived it first: it has done these back-office jobs by hand, then built the agents that do them.

### Live and measured.

A managed AP agent from lumic went live about six weeks after the on-site day. In its first week, 64 of 67 bills went through it. Counted, not estimated.

### Is lumic the right fit?

lumic fits a business with people doing repetitive work by hand, that wants it done inside the systems the team already uses, with a person approving what matters. lumic may not be the right fit for buyers who want a self-serve software license to set up themselves, or an agent that acts with no person approving.

Leadership

### Finance first. Engineers second.

lumic’s leadership includes a controller and a CFP®, based in St. Louis. Its leaders still work in finance, and that is the point: they run real books on the agents lumic deploys. Senior people lead every engagement, on site, from scoping to support.

# Guardrails: approval, logging and access | lumic

> A person approves every entry before it posts, every action is logged, and each agent reaches only what its job needs. The practices on every lumic agent.

Source: https://get-lumic.com/guardrails/ | Contact: hello@get-lumic.com

Guardrails On every agent

# Guardrails: nothing posts without you.

The practices lumic follows on every agent, in one place. A person approves every entry before it posts, every action is logged, and each agent can reach only what its job needs.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) The practices

The practices

## Approval, logging, access and upkeep.

### A person approves every entry.

The agent prepares each entry. A person on your team checks it and approves it before anything posts, and the final post stays in your hands. A person sends every collections email.

### Everything is logged.

Every action an agent takes is logged. A posted payroll entry is logged with its transaction number, and it can’t be posted twice.

### Access is limited to the job.

lumic gives each agent access to the screens and records its job needs, and nothing more. Each agent works under its own login, on its own dedicated computer.

### Paused or revoked any time.

Any agent can be paused, or its access revoked, at any time.

### Dashboards only read.

Dashboards read live from your ERP. Nothing posts from them.

### A cloud AI model reads documents.

To read a document, such as a vendor bill, the agent uses a cloud AI model.

### Watched and tested every month.

Once an agent is live, lumic watches it, tests it every month, fixes what breaks, and upgrades it as AI improves.

### Client data stays under contract.

Data lumic handles for a client is covered by that client’s written agreement with lumic.

The method in full: [How lumic works](https://get-lumic.com/how-lumic-works/). How an agent works inside your systems: [Systems](https://get-lumic.com/systems/). Starting prices: [Pricing](https://get-lumic.com/pricing/). Common questions: [FAQ](https://get-lumic.com/faq/).

# AI agents for the manufacturing back office.

The jobs

## The back-office jobs a manufacturer does by hand.

lumic’s FDEs start beside the person who does each job today, then build one agent per job, inside the systems the plant office already runs. A person approves each entry.

### Vendor bills against purchase orders

The agent reads each vendor bill from email, matches it to the purchase order, and flags a price difference before anyone pays. A person approves it, and nobody retypes it.

- Agent · accounting software
- A person approves each entry

[AP automation →](https://get-lumic.com/services/ap-automation/)

### Job costing during the job

Production data and costs read live, so estimate against actual shows up during the job, not at close.

- Dashboard · production data + ERP
- Overruns surfaced early

### Purchasing and PO write-back

The agent drafts purchase orders and writes them back to the ERP, and a dashboard tracks open POs, receipts and vendor price changes.

- Agent · ERP
- Approval-gated

### Payroll entries

The agent builds the payroll journal entry from the payroll reports, checks every line, and the controller posts it.

- Agent · payroll reports + accounting
- Posted only on the controller’s click

[Payroll →](https://get-lumic.com/services/payroll/)

### Month-end close

The agent prepares the recurring month-end entries and runs the tie-outs. Every entry lands unposted until the controller posts it.

- Agent · ERP
- The controller posts each entry

[Month-end close →](https://get-lumic.com/services/month-end-close/)

### Live margin and cost

Sales and gross margin by customer, product and rep, read live, with the costs the agents enter showing up the same day.

- Dashboard · ERP
- No more morning export

[See examples in production: Portfolio](https://get-lumic.com/portfolio/)

# Forward Deployed Engineers in St. Louis. On site, where the work happens.

How lumic works

## lumic starts where the work happens. Live in weeks, not quarters.

### On-site diagnostic.

lumic’s FDEs work beside your team where the work happens. They map your systems, your data, and the manual steps that take the most time.

### Build the agent.

The team builds an agent for one job, connects it to your systems, and sets up the approval step. Your team tests it on real work before it goes live.

### Managed and kept working.

lumic watches it, tests it, fixes it, and upgrades it, for a monthly fee. You run the business.

# Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) in St. Louis | lumic

> What a Forward Deployed Engineer does for a business, and how lumic's St. Louis FDEs work on site, build inside your systems and stay after launch.

Source: https://get-lumic.com/forward-deployed-engineers/ | Contact: hello@get-lumic.com

Based in St. Louis FDEs for business

# Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) in St. Louis

A forward-deployed engineer (FDE) works on site, builds inside your own systems, and stays to run what was built after launch. A consultant advises and leaves. lumic’s FDEs are based in St. Louis, have finance backgrounds, and build AI into one back-office job at a time.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) FDE or consultant

In plain words

## What is a forward deployed engineer?

A forward deployed engineer (FDE) is an engineer who works on site with a business, inside its own systems. An FDE builds the work there, then stays to run it after launch. lumic’s FDEs have finance backgrounds and build AI into one back-office job at a time.

[FDEs for small and mid-size businesses](https://get-lumic.com/forward-deployed-engineers/small-business/)

FDE or consultant

## A consultant advises. An FDE builds, and stays.

For a business that wants back-office work done by AI, the difference is who is left holding the work after launch. With lumic, it is lumic.

### On site.

lumic’s FDEs work beside your team at your place of business, where the work happens. They map your systems, your data, and the manual steps that take the most time.

### Inside your own systems.

Each agent works on its own dedicated computer, under its own login, inside the systems you already run, whether that’s an ERP, accounting software, email, spreadsheets or cloud apps. No new product to learn.

### Stays after launch.

Once an agent is live, lumic runs it for a monthly fee. The team watches it, tests it every month, fixes what breaks, and upgrades it as AI improves.

### Finance people who code.

Most FDE teams are engineers who learn finance on the job. lumic’s team has done these back-office jobs by hand, then built the agents that do them.

Two ways to bring in AI, side by side.

- A consultant → An FDE from lumic
- Advises from outside → Works on site, beside your team
- Recommends a tool to buy → Builds inside your own systems
- Hands over a plan → Hands over a working agent
- Leaves after the project → Stays to run it after launch

# FAQ: FDEs, AI agents and approvals | lumic

> What an FDE is, where the agent runs, what it can touch, who approves its work, how long it takes to go live, and how lumic prices a job.

Source: https://get-lumic.com/faq/ | Contact: hello@get-lumic.com

FAQ Common questions

# Common questions about lumic.

What an FDE is, where the agent runs, what it can touch, who approves its work, how long it takes to go live, and how lumic prices a job.

Questions

## Plain answers.

### What is an FDE?

FDE stands for Forward Deployed Engineer. lumic's FDEs are engineers with finance backgrounds who come to you, learn how the work is really done, build AI into one job at a time, and keep it working.

### Where does the agent run?

Wherever fits your business, on its own dedicated computer, under its own login, inside the systems you already run, whether that's an ERP, accounting software, email, spreadsheets or cloud apps. To read a document, it uses a cloud AI model.

### What can the agent touch?

Only what its job needs. lumic gives each agent access to the screens and records its job needs, and nothing more. Every action it takes is logged.

### Who approves what the agent does?

A person on your team. The agent makes the entry, and a person checks it and approves it before anything posts. The final post stays in your hands.

### How long does it take to go live?

Weeks, not quarters. A recent managed AP agent went live about six weeks after the on-site day; in its first week, 64 of 67 bills went through the agent.

### What does it cost?

It depends on the job. The consultation is free, and on-site work is $1,500/day, credited toward phase one. Managed agents from $1,000/month; full build-and-run from $2,500–6,000/month. The build is a separate, one-time cost, scoped after the free consultation. These figures are starting points, not quotes. Details: [Pricing](https://get-lumic.com/pricing/).

### Do you work outside St. Louis?

Yes. St. Louis first: the team is based here and comes on site in person. lumic travels for the right fit.

### Does lumic sell software?

No. lumic does not sell software to configure yourself; the team stays to run what it builds.

### What happens after an agent goes live?

lumic runs it for a monthly fee. The team watches it, tests it every month, fixes what breaks, and upgrades it as AI improves. A person on your team approves anything before it posts.

### What systems does lumic work with?

If your team runs it, lumic can work with it, whether that's an ERP, accounting software, email, spreadsheets or cloud apps. The home page [lists the systems](https://get-lumic.com/#systems).

### Is lumic the right fit?

lumic fits a business with people doing repetitive work by hand, that wants it done inside the systems the team already uses, with a person approving what matters. lumic may not be the right fit for buyers who want a self-serve software license to set up themselves, or an agent that acts with no person approving.

The method in full: [How lumic works](https://get-lumic.com/how-lumic-works/). One agent, step by step: [AP automation](https://get-lumic.com/services/ap-automation/). Every agent and dashboard: [Portfolio](https://get-lumic.com/portfolio/).

Systems QuickBooks

# AI agents that work in QuickBooks Online and QuickBooks Desktop.

lumic works with QuickBooks Online and QuickBooks Desktop. An agent prepares bills, receipts and entries in QuickBooks, the same records a clerk would key, and a person approves before anything posts. lumic builds it on site and keeps it working.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) See the jobs

Online and Desktop

## Both editions, one way of working.

Many automation tools reach only QuickBooks Online. lumic’s agents work wherever your books live.

### QuickBooks Online

The agent works with your QuickBooks Online company through its own login, and prepares each entry for a person to approve.

- Cloud edition
- A person approves each entry

### QuickBooks Desktop

The agent works on its own dedicated computer, under its own login, inside the QuickBooks Desktop company file your team already uses.

- Desktop edition
- Its own computer and login

### Alongside QuickBooks

Bills arrive by email, purchase orders may live in another system, and reports end up in spreadsheets. The agent works across the tools around your books, not just inside them.

- Email, spreadsheets, other systems
- One job, end to end

Vendor bills

## Vendor bills in QuickBooks Desktop

The agent reads each vendor bill, matches it to the purchase order, and enters the bill in QuickBooks Desktop once a person approves it. When the purchase orders live in a separate operations database, it enters the bill there too, so nobody types it twice.

### It reads each bill.

The agent reads each vendor bill as it arrives by email, the same bill a clerk would open.

### It matches the PO.

It matches the bill to the purchase order and flags a price difference before anyone pays.

### A person approves, then it enters.

After a person approves it, the agent enters the bill in QuickBooks Desktop, and in the operations database that holds the purchase orders when there is one.

The jobs

## What an agent does in QuickBooks.

### Vendor bills.

The agent reads each vendor bill from email, matches it to the purchase order, and prepares the bill in QuickBooks for a person to approve. [AP automation](https://get-lumic.com/services/ap-automation/)

### Cash receipts and collections.

Remittances read and keyed as receipts for approval, and collections emails drafted from live aging for a person to send. [Cash receipts and collections](https://get-lumic.com/services/cash-receipts-and-collections/)

### Live reports.

Sales, margin and receivables read live from QuickBooks, so nobody exports the same report every morning. [Dashboards and reporting](https://get-lumic.com/services/dashboards-and-reporting/)

Nothing posts without you.

# Sage 100 AP automation with an AI agent | lumic

> An agent reads each vendor bill, matches it to the PO and prepares the invoice and receipt in Sage 100. A person reviews and posts.

Source: https://get-lumic.com/systems/sage-100/ap-automation/ | Contact: hello@get-lumic.com

Sage 100 AP automation

# Sage 100 AP automation, with a person posting every batch.

An agent reads each vendor bill, matches it to the purchase order, and prepares the AP invoice and the PO receipt in Sage 100, in an unposted batch. A person on your team reviews the batch and posts it. lumic builds it on site and keeps it working.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/lumic/20-minute-call) See the job

The job, step by step

## From the inbox to an unposted batch. A person posts it.

### A bill arrives by email.

The agent reads each vendor bill as it arrives by email, the same bill a clerk would open.

### It matches the PO.

It matches the bill to the purchase order in Sage 100.

### It prepares the batch.

It prepares the AP invoice and the PO receipt in an unposted Sage 100 batch, ready for a person to review.

Flags

## Flags before anyone pays.

When a bill does not match, the agent flags it for a person before it goes into the batch.

### Price off the PO

The bill’s price is not the price on the purchase order. The agent flags the difference for a person to approve.

- Flagged before anyone pays

### Quantity off the PO

The bill charges for more or less than the purchase order. The agent flags it for a person to check.

- Flagged before anyone pays

### A duplicate invoice number

The vendor’s invoice number is already in Sage 100. The agent flags it, so the same bill is not paid twice.

- Flagged before anyone pays

Access

## Its own computer, its own login.

### Its own computer and login.

The agent works on its own dedicated computer, under its own login, inside the Sage 100 your team already uses.

### Access scoped to AP.

lumic gives the agent access to the AP screens and records its job needs, and nothing more.

### Every action logged.

Every action the agent takes is logged.

The post stays with you.

### A person posts every batch.

The agent prepares the batch and leaves it unposted. A person on your team reviews it and posts it. The final post stays in your hands.

### Nothing posts without you.

The agent never posts the batch itself. Flagged bills wait for a person’s approval.

The AP job on any system: [AP automation](https://get-lumic.com/services/ap-automation/). Every job an agent does with Sage 100: [Sage 100](https://get-lumic.com/systems/sage-100/). Starting prices: [Pricing](https://get-lumic.com/pricing/).

Questions

## Sage 100 AP automation, in plain answers.

### Can AI work with Sage 100?

Yes. A lumic agent works with Sage 100 on its own dedicated computer, under its own login. It reads each vendor bill, matches it to the PO, and prepares the AP invoice and PO receipt in an unposted batch. A person reviews the batch and posts it.

# Month-End Red Flags Service Firms Usually Miss | lumic

> Ten month-end mistakes in AP, billing, payroll and the close, on one page: a free checklist from lumic, with a PDF download.

Source: https://get-lumic.com/resources/month-end-red-flags/ | Contact: hello@get-lumic.com

Checklist Month-end

# Month-End Red Flags Service Firms Usually Miss

A short checklist for engineering firms, staffing firms, construction services and agencies. Each item is a habit that quietly slows the close or leaks margin. Count how many sound familiar.

[Download the PDF](https://get-lumic.com/resources/month-end-red-flags.pdf)

## Ten red flags.

### Unbilled time sitting past month-end.

Hours logged but not invoiced by the last day mean revenue lands a month late and cash follows even later.

### Vendor bills keyed twice, or not at all.

Bills arriving by email, portal and paper get entered by hand. Duplicates slip through, and missing ones show up as surprises after the close.

### Subcontractor and pass-through costs not matched to the job.

Costs that never get tagged to a project or client make job margin look better (or worse) than it is.

### Payroll journal entries built from a spreadsheet.

Copying payroll reports into an entry by hand invites misallocated wages, burden and accruals, especially across departments or jobs.

### Accrued payroll ignored at cutoff.

When a pay period crosses month-end and wages are not accrued, labor cost swings from month to month for no real reason.

### Cash receipts posted in a lump.

Deposits applied "on account" instead of to specific invoices leave aging reports wrong and collections chasing clients who already paid.

### Collections that start at 60 days.

Without a steady, polite reminder at the first missed due date, receivables age quietly while the team is busy delivering work.

### Recurring entries rebuilt every month.

Prepaids, depreciation, rent and software accruals typed fresh each close are slow and easy to get wrong.

### Tie-outs skipped when the close runs late.

Bank, AP, AR and payroll clearing accounts not reconciled before reports go out means leadership decides on numbers that will change.

### Reports exported and rebuilt by hand.

If revenue, margin and receivables come from a weekly export, the numbers are already stale when someone reads them.

Every one of these is a job an agent can take on. lumic builds AI agents that prepare bills, receipts, payroll entries and month-end entries in the systems a firm already runs, and a person approves each entry before anything posts.
